From f3c6aa078927e6fe8121c9c591ddee8716c5305a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Til Kaiser <mail@tk154.de>
Date: Sun, 7 Jun 2026 15:49:41 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] net: mvpp2: limit XDP frame size to the RX buffer

mvpp2 has short and long BM pools, and short pool buffers can be smaller
than PAGE_SIZE. The XDP path nevertheless initializes every xdp_buff with
PAGE_SIZE as frame size.

XDP helpers use frame_sz to validate tail growth and to derive the hard
end of the data area. Advertising PAGE_SIZE for short buffers can let
bpf_xdp_adjust_tail() grow a packet past the real allocation, corrupting
memory or later tripping skb tailroom checks.

Initialize the XDP buffer with bm_pool->frag_size so XDP tailroom matches
the actual buffer backing the packet.

Fixes: 07dd0a7aae7f ("mvpp2: add basic XDP support")
Signed-off-by: Til Kaiser <mail@tk154.de>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260607134943.21996-3-mail@tk154.de
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/marvell/mvpp2/mvpp2_main.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/marvell/mvpp2/mvpp2_main.c
index 92a701f4fe3f..3372ed27cc8d 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/marvell/mvpp2/mvpp2_main.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/marvell/mvpp2/mvpp2_main.c
@@ -3979,7 +3979,7 @@ static int mvpp2_rx(struct mvpp2_port *port, struct napi_struct *napi,
 			else
 				xdp_rxq = &rxq->xdp_rxq_long;
 
-			xdp_init_buff(&xdp, PAGE_SIZE, xdp_rxq);
+			xdp_init_buff(&xdp, bm_pool->frag_size, xdp_rxq);
 			xdp_prepare_buff(&xdp, data,
 					 MVPP2_MH_SIZE + MVPP2_SKB_HEADROOM,
 					 rx_bytes, true);
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the patch

This patch fixes an XDP frame size mismatch in the Marvell mvpp2 network driver.

### Files modified

- **`drivers/net/ethernet/marvell/mvpp2/mvpp2_main.c`**  
  In the `mvpp2_rx()` function, the call to `xdp_init_buff()` was changed from using `PAGE_SIZE` as the frame size to using the actual buffer size `bm_pool->frag_size`.

### Relationship between modifications

The single change addresses the root cause of the bug: the XDP buffer was initialised with a frame size (`PAGE_SIZE`) larger than the actual memory allocated for the packet (which can be smaller when using short buffer pools). This mismatch allowed `bpf_xdp_adjust_tail()` to grow the packet beyond the real buffer, leading to memory corruption or incorrect tailroom checks. By feeding the correct `frag_size` from the buffer pool, the XDP framework now respects the true buffer boundaries, preventing overruns.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
- `xdp_init_buff(&xdp, PAGE_SIZE, xdp_rxq);`

Reason:
In the XDP path, the XDP buffer was initialized with a frame size of `PAGE_SIZE` regardless of the actual buffer pool size. Short buffer pools (e.g., `bm_pool->frag_size` smaller than `PAGE_SIZE`) are used, so `bpf_xdp_adjust_tail()` could grow a packet beyond the real buffer allocation, causing memory corruption or later tailroom checks to fail. The frame size defines the maximum tailroom allowed; using `PAGE_SIZE` for small buffers overestimates the available space.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
- `xdp_init_buff(&xdp, bm_pool->frag_size, xdp_rxq);`

Reason:
By using `bm_pool->frag_size` (the actual fragment size of the buffer pool) instead of `PAGE_SIZE`, the XDP buffer’s frame size correctly reflects the real allocation. This restricts `bpf_xdp_adjust_tail()` to only grow the packet within the bounds of the actual buffer, preventing memory corruption and ensuring proper tailroom checks. The fix aligns the XDP frame size with the buffer pool’s true size.
